claims.text: The starting material is a homogeneous solution or solid mixture of noble-metal single-source precursors.
Restricting precursor atomic mobility during reduction produces kinetic trapping.
Restricted mobility forces stochastic incorporation of different metal atoms into nucleating nanoparticles.
Stochastic incorporation favors homogeneous, single-phase high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
Conditions permitting greater atomic mobility cause phase separation or elemental segregation.
Lower processing temperatures restrict atomic or precursor mobility.
Rapid quenching restricts atomic or precursor mobility in this synthesis.
Fast reduction kinetics slow atomic diffusion or otherwise reduce precursor mobility.
Atomic mobility controls whether constituent atoms become trapped in a random lattice or reorganize into segregated phases.
Sequential or consecutive reduction events promote random incorporation of multiple metals.
Random incorporation overcomes thermodynamic driving forces for phase separation.
At high mobility, thermodynamically driven aggregation or phase segregation prevails.
Restricted-mobility synthesis will predominantly yield single-phase homogeneous nanoparticles with randomly distributed constituents.
Relative to the baseline, restricted mobility will reduce phase-separated domains and elemental segregation.
The higher-mobility baseline will have more uncontrolled nanoparticle morphologies.
The hypothesis is intended to apply to noble-metal HEA nanoparticles made from single-source precursors under low-temperature reduction protocols.
The hypothesis may not apply to high-temperature routes in which thermodynamics dominate kinetic trapping.
Non-noble metals or different precursor chemistries may introduce mechanisms outside the proposed mobility-controlled regime.
The quantitative mobility threshold and the effect of ligand chemistry may vary between systems.
Failure of restricted-mobility conditions to produce a statistically significant increase in homogeneous single-phase alloy formation relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.
